thought.text: ES is extracted. Now configure it (ES refuses to run as root, so I'll create a dedicated user).

reasoning_content: Extraction complete. Next, set up ES. ES cannot be run as root, so a user is required. Create the `elastic` user, set up configuration (single node, no security, heap 2g), and start it.

action.command:
useradd -r -m -d /opt/elasticsearch -s /bin/bash elastic 2>/dev/null; chown -R elastic:elastic /opt/downloads/elasticsearch-7.17.28 && mv /opt/downloads/elasticsearch-7.17.28 /opt/elasticsearch && ln -sfn /opt/elasticsearch /opt/es; cat > /opt/elasticsearch/config/elasticsearch.yml <<'EOF'
cluster.name: index-data-explorer
node.name: node-1
path.data: /opt/elasticsearch/data
path.logs: /opt/elasticsearch/logs
network.host: 127.0.0.1
http.port: 9200
discovery.type: single-node
EOF
chown elastic:elastic /opt/elasticsearch/config/elasticsearch.yml
echo "ES_DIR:"; ls /opt/elasticsearch/bin/elasticsearch && /opt/elasticsearch/bin/elasticsearch --version 2>/dev/null | head -2
